incidents.name: PLA token minter-role key compromise
incidents.notes: The PLA token's owner key was compromised and used to grant the minter role to a fresh attacker address, which then called mint() for 1.79 billion PLA across four transactions; the token's access control worked as written and no code flaw was involved.

sources.ref: onchain review: PLA token 0x3a4f40631a4f906c2bad353ed06de7a5d3fcb430 created 2020-04-22 by PlayDapp deployer 0x6f53e6f92e85c084e10aaf35d4a44dee6a27892d, no upgrade events; the first unauthorized mint (100,000,000 PLA) is signed by the fresh EOA 0xd151050d43c28690766f50ce9ea8686c5d243a40. lossUsd uses the ~$32m the attacker actually converted (Nefture; cryptonews) rather than the $290m nominal value of the minted supply.
